![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14057748/assets/204afb23fc438b047c72d6233b59b70c4741ee16a30a57c084682a3d14fd2188.png)

A thin soap film is stretching over time. The graph of its surface area $A(t)$, in square centimeters, after $t$ minutes is shown above. Approximate the rate of change of the surface area at $t=2$ using a forward difference with step size $h=2.$ Do not round the answer.

After $2$ minutes, the surface area increases at a rate of {{field-1}} ${\text{cm}}^{2}/\text{min}.$
worked_solution:
We use the forward difference approximation

$$
{A}^{′}(t)≈\frac{A(t+h)-A(t)}{h},
$$

at the time $t=2$ with step size $h=2.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{′}(2) & ≈\frac{A(2+2)-A(2)}{2} \\  & =\frac{A(4)-A(2)}{2} \\  & =\frac{40-10}{2} \\  & =15.\end{aligned}
$$

So, after $2$ minutes, the surface area changes at a rate of approximately $15\text{ }{\text{cm}}^{2}/\text{min}.$
